title: Capacity-safe rolling upgrade controller for dedicated GPU pools (drain + autoscaler coordination)
creator: Samira Patel
description:
Goal: Build a capacity-safe rolling upgrade controller for Dedicated GPU pools that coordinates controlled GPU node draining, autoscaler policies, and rollout gates so upgrades never exhaust serving capacity or violate latency SLOs.

Scope: implement controller logic + API to schedule pool upgrades, integrate with autoscaler to temporarily suspend scale-downs and reserve burst capacity, expose rollout status to Console, add rollout gates (pre-checks, canary, health gates), and add observability and rollback criteria. This ticket focuses on the pool-level orchestration and runbook; separate tickets will cover node image builders and infra provisioning.

Key requirements:
- Graceful drain mechanism: move new requests off targeted nodes, gracefully close/evict long-lived KV caches, flush/serialize in-flight KV segments for later reuse.
- Autoscaler coordination: when an upgrade begins, autoscaler must not remove spare nodes; controller requests a temporary "upgrade-reservation" to hold X% extra capacity per pool and prevents aggressive scale-in until drains complete.
- Concurrency control: configurable max concurrent node reboots per pool and per-GPU-type so we never reduce available slots below a safety threshold.
- Health & rollout gates: preflight checks (available spare slots, model kernel compatibility, quantization profile availability), canary subset rollout (single rack / AZ), automated gating on SLO signals (increased 95p latency, error-rate, queue length) with configurable thresholds and automatic pause/rollback.
- Visibility: surface per-pool rollout progress and gate states in Console (per-route token throughput, 95p/99p serving latency, failed requests, queue length, GPU utilization) and streaming logs/events for each node transition.
- Testing & verification: synthetic traffic with realistic token distributions, soak tests for long-running sessions, and simulated autoscaler events to validate controller coordination.

Design trade-offs discussed: prefer strong safety (lower concurrency) by default to minimize regressions vs. slower rollouts for large fleets; expose knobs for customers on Dedicated to opt-into more aggressive/fast upgrades. We decided to require both a preflight check and a canary gate before full rollout to balance speed and safety.

Acceptance criteria:
- Controller can schedule and execute an upgrade across a GPU pool with no more than configured X% capacity reduction at any time.
- Autoscaler honors temporary reservation requests and does not scale in below reservation during upgrade.
- Console shows live rollout state and gate triggers for at least one dedicated customer in staging.
- Automated rollback triggers on breach of configured SLO thresholds and performs policy-driven fallback to previous model/runtime variant.

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Dedicated+Rolling+Upgrades+Design
- Console mockups: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/console-dedicated-rollout-mocks
- Draft PR for upgrade-controller prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1718
- E2E test harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-tests/tree/main/upgrade-tests

Next steps (implementation tasks):
1) Upgrade controller service skeleton + API for scheduling (ENG task A).
2) Autoscaler API extension: reservation token and scale-in hold (ENG task B).
3) Drain library improvements: KV cache checkpoint/restore hooks + quiet window semantics (ENG task C).
4) Console integration: rollout timeline and gate event panels (ENG task D).
5) E2E automation: synthetic loads, canary automation, rollback simulation (ENG task E).

Runbook highlights (for oncall):
- Pause criteria: 95p latency > configured threshold for 2 consecutive 1m windows OR error-rate doubles vs baseline for 3 minutes.
- Automatic rollback: triggered if pause persists > 10m and manual unpause not approved.
- Emergency stop: CLI command to abort and drainback new traffic.

Notes: this ticket touches infra APIs and will require a security review because reservation requests could affect tenancy isolation and billing. Coordinate with security and billing teams before enabling for high-usage enterprise customers.
